The VFS has two distinct duplication paths: descriptor `dup`/`dup2` share one reference-counted `struct file`, while internal `file_dup2` copies `f_priv` into a new file and calls the driver’s `open` method. I’ll give that internal reopen its own copy of the immutable snapshot, avoiding a driver refcount or shared allocation lifetime.

The candidate captures text at open and keeps it through partial reads, EOF, zero-length reads and rewinds. A new independent open gets fresh text. I’ve also added a small seek callback that preserves the old SET/CUR behavior and unsupported SEEK_END, while serializing offsets with reads through shared descriptors.

The host regression reproduces the old corruption: a 1,174-byte report becomes a mixed 1,181-byte stream when a field grows between reads. The fixed functions pass byte-for-byte checks across changing counters, concurrent readers/opens, dup and close ordering, failure paths and seeks. I’ll read the full E77 work order and the frozen driver’s notification and initialization paths, then implement the bounded STA event task. I’ll check wakeup races, down/up handling, ownership and resource costs offline, and prepare the E77 build/controller handoff for Root.

The old TX service body already serializes with RX, timeout and interface teardown through the device mutex. I’ll retain that body and change only how STA notifications reach it. The current LPWORK settings are priority 100 and a 2048-byte stack; I’m checking task allocation and failure cleanup before choosing the event/task state.

The event state keeps one wake reservation set until the task consumes and claims it. Down clears pending work but preserves that reservation, because its producer may still be about to post outside the lock. A fresh event after re-up can reuse it. Each claimed event runs one unchanged service batch, then releases the device mutex and yields; ENOMEM alone causes no self-post.
